title: Isomorphisms and proper finite presentation under flat deformation
statement: Use algebraic spaces over a scheme $S$ and their small etale sites and structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A first order thickening $Z\hookrightarrow Z\prime$ means a representable closed immersion whose ideal sheaf has square zero and whose underlying closed subset is all of $Z\prime$; closed immersion is tested after every scheme base change, closed immersions of schemes being [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $B\hookrightarrow B\prime$ be a first order thickening. Let $P\prime\to B\prime$ and $Q\prime\to B\prime$ be algebraic spaces over $B\prime$, with $P\prime$ flat over $B\prime$, and let $h\prime:P\prime\to Q\prime$ be a $B\prime$-morphism. Put $P=B\times_{B\prime}P\prime$, $Q=B\times_{B\prime}Q\prime$ and $h=h\prime|_P:P\to Q$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Then $h\prime$ is an isomorphism if and only if $h$ is; $h\prime$ is proper if and only if $h$ is; and $h\prime$ is finitely presented if and only if $h$ is. Here flat and locally of finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finitely presented means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation. Proper means separated, quasi-compact, locally of finite type on etale charts, and universally closed. Quasi-separated means the diagonal is quasi-compact; separated means the diagonal is a closed immersion; universally closed means closed after every algebraic-space base change (the scheme conventions are [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]).

source.place: Tag 0CG6 (lemma-deform-property), parts (3), (5), (7), (14), (21); the finite presentation assertion is (5)+(7)+(14).

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $U\prime\to B\prime$, then a surjective etale scheme atlas $V\prime\to Q\prime\times_{B\prime}U\prime$, and then $W\prime\to P\prime\times_{Q\prime}V\prime$. The cited fibre-product and representable-etale permanence statements make $W\prime\to P\prime\times_{B\prime}U\prime$, and hence $W\prime\to P\prime$, surjective etale. Put $U,V,W$ for their pullbacks to $B$. Since flatness is preserved by base change, $P\prime\times_{B\prime}U\prime\to U\prime$ is flat; the chart test, with target chart the identity of $U\prime$, gives flatness of $W\prime\to U\prime$. The same chart test detects local finite type and local finite presentation of $h\prime$ on $W\prime\to V\prime$, and of $h$ on $W\to V$. Work affine-locally in these schemes, writing the compatible coordinate maps as $R\prime\to A\prime\to C\prime$. The square-zero base ideal $I\subseteq R\prime$ gives $R=R\prime/I$, $A=A\prime/IA\prime$, $C=C\prime/IC\prime$ by the quotient base-change statement. Moreover $C\prime$ is flat over $R\prime$ by the affine flatness criterion. These choices may be refined at every point, so no quasi-compact atlas is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0CG6 (lemma-deform-property), choice of U prime, V prime, W prime; affine coordinate reduction as in Tag 06AG, general remark (I).

proof.text: The maps $P\to P\prime$ and $Q\to Q\prime$ are thickenings by base change of $B\to B\prime$. Also $P=Q\times_{Q\prime}P\prime$: on a test scheme both sides consist of a point of $P\prime$ together with its lift of the base point to $B$. Thus the square $(h,h\prime)$ is a morphism of thickenings. Apply the topological-properties statement separately to quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, separation and universal closedness. Each holds for $h$ if and only if it holds for $h\prime$. The first-order condition needed later holds on every scheme chart since $(IA\prime)^2=I^2A\prime=0$, and likewise for $C\prime$; it needs no flatness of $Q\prime$.

Apply the cartesian finite-order thickening local-finite-type statement to $W\prime\to V\prime$ and its pullback $W\to V$. The target thickening $V\to V\prime$ is first order, and $W=V\times_{V\prime}W\prime$ by the preceding cartesian identification. It follows that $W\prime\to V\prime$ is locally of finite type exactly when $W\to V$ is. Applying the chart test to the two pairs of atlases gives the same equivalence for $h\prime$ and $h$.

source.place: Tag 09ZZ (lemma-thicken-property-morphisms-cartesian), part (2), reduction to schemes; scheme result Tag 09ZW, part (2).

proof.text: On the affine refinements in step 1, the relative finite-presentation lifting lemma applies to $R\prime\to A\prime\to C\prime$: $I^2=0$ and $C\prime$ is $R\prime$-flat. It equates finite presentation of $A\prime\to C\prime$ with that of $A\to C$. For a locally finitely presented scheme morphism its ring map on every compatible pair of affine opens is finitely presented, by the cited affine-opens statement. Consequently local finite presentation of $W\to V$ implies it for $W\prime\to V\prime$ on all the affine refinements; conversely local finite presentation of $W\prime\to V\prime$ implies it for $W\to V$ using the reverse implication of the same algebra lemma. The affine definition and the chart test then give $h\prime$ locally of finite presentation if and only if $h$ is. The argument does not assume $A\prime$ flat over $R\prime$.

source.place: Tag 0CG6, clause (14), source-and-target etale-chart reduction to Tag 06AG, clause (13).

proof.text: Combine step 2 with step 3: the four conditions in the stated definition of properness (separated, quasi-compact, locally of finite type and universally closed) are each equivalent for $h$ and $h\prime$. Their conjunction proves the properness equivalence. Combine step 2 with step 4: quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness and local finite presentation are each equivalent, so their conjunction proves the finite-presentation equivalence.

source.place: Tag 0CG6, clause (21), and clauses (5), (7), (14); definitions of proper and finitely presented in the item.

proof.text: Assume now that $h$ is an isomorphism. Then $P\times_QV\cong V$, so $W\to V$ is etale by the representable scheme-test statement. In particular it is flat and locally of finite presentation. Step 4, applied on these charts, gives local finite presentation of $W\prime\to V\prime$. On every affine refinement as in step 1, $C$ is flat over $A$ by the affine flatness criterion. Apply the nilpotent-fibre module criterion with base ring $R\prime$, intermediate ring $A\prime$, module $C\prime$, and ideal $I$: $C\prime$ is $R\prime$-flat by step 1, and $C\prime/IC\prime=C$ is flat over $A\prime/IA\prime=A$. Thus $C\prime$ is flat over $A\prime$. The affine criterion gives flatness of $W\prime\to V\prime$.

source.place: Tag 0CG6, etale-chart argument for clause (20), then clause (3); flatness input algebra.tex Tag 06A5.

proof.text: For any $v\prime\in V\prime$, the square-zero ideal of $V\subseteq V\prime$ vanishes in the field $\kappa(v\prime)$: the square of the image of each of its elements is zero in a field. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v\prime)\to V\prime$ factors through $V$. The cartesian square identifies the fibre of $W\prime\to V\prime$ there with the base change of $W\to V$ to this field. It is etale by the cited etale base-change statement. Apply the flat-fibre etale-neighbourhood criterion to $W\prime\to V\prime$, which is flat and locally of finite presentation by step 6. Every point of $W\prime$ has an open neighbourhood etale over $V\prime$. Etale source locality then gives that $W\prime\to V\prime$ is etale.

The composite $W\prime\to V\prime\to Q\prime$ is representable etale by step 7 and representable-etale composition. Since $W\prime\to P\prime$ is a representable surjective etale atlas (step 1), the source-atlas detection statement makes $h\prime$ chartwise etale. Its pullback by the thickening $Q\to Q\prime$ is exactly $h$, by step 2, so the etale-thickening detection statement makes $h\prime$ an isomorphism. Conversely, if $h\prime$ is an isomorphism, pulling back its inverse along $Q\to Q\prime$ gives the inverse of $h$, since the two inverse equations are preserved by the fibre-product universal property.

source.place: Tag 0CG6, clause (3), using etaleness and surjectivity; equivalent final detection by Tag 05ZH (theorem-topological-invariance).

lean.statement: theorem flat_deformation_properties {S : Scheme.{u}} {B B' : AlgebraicSpace S} (i : B ⟶ B') (hi : IsSpaceFirstOrderThickening i) {P' Q' : Over B'} (h' : P' ⟶ Q') (hflat : MapIsFlat P'.hom) : (IsIso h'.left ↔ IsIso (flatDeformationMap i h')) ∧ (MapIsProper h'.left ↔ MapIsProper (flatDeformationMap i h')) ∧ ((MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation h'.left ∧ MapIsQuasiCompact h'.left.hom.hom ∧ MapIsQuasiCompact (pullback.diagonal h'.left.hom.hom)) ↔ (MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation (flatDeformationMap i h') ∧ MapIsQuasiCompact (flatDeformationMap i h').hom.hom ∧ MapIsQuasiCompact (pullback.diagonal (flatDeformationMap i h').hom.hom)))
lean.note: The slice morphism encodes precisely a B-prime morphism. flatDeformationMap is its concrete map of sheaf pullbacks, induced by the identity of B and the given morphism; finite presentation is expanded as lfp, quasi-compact and quasi-compact diagonal. Reuses the landed definition owners def-sfb-space-square-zero-extension-data, def-sfb-space-morphism-properties, def-sfb-space-sheaf-fibre-product and def-sfb-proper-curve-moduli without defining another notion.
